subject: Private deployment: edge gateway handoff & SLA delegation request
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helioslabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@gcp-partner.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: latency spikes at edge handoff — request for SLA exception

Hi Marissa / Naomi,

Hope youre well. Were seeing intermittent 200-400ms tail latency spikes for inference requests originating from our edge gateways in our VPC region (us-west-2). These spikes correlate with our CDN/CDN-to-VPC handoff windows and a third-party transit provider change on Jan 9. Attached is a short extract of network flows from Jan 10-11 (network-flows-jan11.log).

Because Helios manages the edge gateways (NAT and TLS offload) and we run a third-party CDN in front of the gateway, wed like to request a formal exception to the Redwood Private SLA that attributes such edge/CDN-caused latency to the customer side. Specifically were asking:
- confirmation that Redwood will exclude latency proven to be beyond the customer gateway from availability/latency SLO calculations, and
- a short, signed exception document we can attach to our compliance pack for an upcoming audit.

We can provide packet captures, traceroutes, and CDN timestamps if that helps. Can we get a quick triage and an outline of what evidence Redwood needs to accept an exception? Were hoping to close this before our compliance review next week.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Infra, Helios Labs
S: +1 415 555 0192

---
Attachment: network-flows-jan11.log (text/log excerpt, 48KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: latency spikes at edge handoff — request for SLA exception

Thanks for the details, Sanjay — appreciate the quick sample.

Short answer: we can work with you on a carve-out for latency that is demonstrably caused by customer-side edge/CDN/transit. To do that we need a reproducible evidence set and an operational agreement that specifies who controls which hops.

What well need from you to evaluate the exception request:
- synchronized traces (UTC timestamps), including CDN request timestamps and the first hop into the customer gateway;
- packet captures or PCAP slices around the spike windows;
- traceroute/mtr output from the edge gateway to the Redwood ingress;
- confirmation of any NAT/load-balancer pre-processing (TLS offload, TCP proxy) and the config that generates client-visible latency;
- KMS usage logs if the handoff triggers key operations that add latency.

From Redwood we can:
- provide a traceroute/handshake sample from our ingress, and the exact timestamp markers we use to compute our inference latency SLO;
- run a correlated 1-hour capture on our side if you provide a maintenance window;
- draft a limited SLA carve-out that names the specific handoff boundary and the evidence required to attribute latency to the customer side.

Looping in Karthik for a technical apportionment and Logan for monitoring hooks, and Naomi for the compliance implications. Suggest a short working call tomorrow to align on the evidence format and the exception text. Are you available Tue 12 Jan 0900-1100 PST?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Account Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: latency spikes at edge handoff — request for SLA exception

Thanks — quick technical summary from ops side. Ill keep this high level.

What Redwood controls on Private deployments:
- the inference runtime latency once a request enters our ingress (TLS termination point under the customers VPC peering/privatelink configuration),
- internal queuing/batching and GPU execution,
- service-side routing and internal retries.

What is generally customer/third-party controlled:
- any client-visible latency caused by edge gateways, CDN caching/handoff, transit-provider peering, and upstream TLS proxying;
- DNS resolution timeouts and edge-side rate-limiting prior to our ingress.

Proposed apportionment approach (operational detail):
- Redwoods 95th percentile inference latency SLO will exclude requests where customer-provided evidence shows the extra latency occurred before the first packet hit the identified gateway egress interface.
- Evidence consists of at least two independent correlated artifacts (e.g., CDN timestamp + traceroute + PCAP) with matching UTC windows and request IDs.
- For mixed-path cases (partial overlap), we propose assigning latency to the party that contributed >50% of the observed tail (by time-series comparison).

We can draft a one-page responsibility matrix and a short evidence checklist. Im attaching a proposed template matrix we often use internally — this will show the handoff boundary and who must provide which logs.

-Karthik

---
Attachment: handoff-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helioslabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@gcp-partner.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: latency spikes at edge handoff — request for SLA exception

Thanks Karthik — that apportionment approach makes sense. A couple quick follow-ups:

1) Our CDN inserts request IDs but they trim certain headers. Will Redwood accept an encrypted request ID or timestamp alignment instead of a full request-id match?
2) For the >50% attribution rule, what baseline window do you use (p50/p95/p99)? Wed like to avoid a rule that uses p99 bursts to blame the customer for short-lived transient spikes.

We can provide PCAPs and CDN logs for the flagged windows. Also, were evaluating a temporary mitigation (disable CDN edge TCP pooling for a weekend) and would like to request a one-off SLA credit/waiver if the mitigation doesnt materially reduce spikes — the audit timeline is tight and we need something to show the compliance team.

Would Redwood legal accept a 30-day timeboxed exception with logging obligations on our side and the right for Redwood to verify config changes? Happy to take a draft and sign it.

Sanjay

---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@helioslabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: latency spikes at edge handoff — request for SLA exception

Sanjay — thanks for the collaboration and for providing the initial traces. Legal has reviewed the apportionment language and we can agree to a timeboxed, evidence-backed carve-out with the following key points: 

- Scope: exception applies to latency that is demonstrably attributable to customer-managed edge gateways, third-party CDNs, or transit peering that occur before the packet reaches the named gateway interface.
- Evidence: Helios must produce at least two independent artifacts per incident (e.g., CDN timestamp + traceroute or PCAP slices with matching UTC timestamps). Redwood reserves the right to request additional captures for verification.
- Attribution rule: we will use comparative time-series over the flagged window; latency will be assigned to the party accounting for the majority of extra tail latency. We will default to p95 for sustained tail attribution; p99-only microbursts under 30s will not by themselves trigger carve-outs unless supported by PCAP/traceroute evidence.
- Duration & credits: we can issue a 30-day exception window starting on sign‑date. If Helios performs the proposed mitigation and the issue persists (per verified evidence), Redwood will consider a one-off usage credit on a case-by-case basis; credits are limited to impacted request volume and require sign-off from Redwood GTM.
- Operational obligations: Helios agrees to maintain capture windows and to notify Redwood of configuration changes that could affect handoff behavior. Redwood will provide monitoring hooks (timestamp formats, trace ID templates) and an ingress-side capture we can use for correlation.

Ive attached a short exception template for signature; if youre good with this we can execute and open the 30-day window. Please review and let us know if you need changes to the p95/p99 language.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
